problems.source_says: Table E reports separate completion rates for the headline, primary text, and description. It does not report counts of ideas, distinct categories, or unique ideas, as category_count is defined in codebook section 6. The paper does not explain the completion-rate calculation or coding procedure, so this measure code is unsupported; retain the completion-rate description and leave the measure code null rather than inventing a counting method.
problems.quote: Participants in human-AI teams had consistently higher completion rates for all ad copy elements (headline, primary text, and description)
problems.locator: PDF p. 48, Appendix E (Ad Copy Completion); p. 49, Table E; pp. 22-23, Section 4.1; creativity-codebook.md section 6, Measure.

problems.source_says: The field sample contains 2,000 ads before exclusions, but Tables 3 and I report 4,997 VTD observations. Equation 2 describes outcomes for ad t in campaign c, which supports the stated ad-level model but does not explain what the 4,997 actual analysis rows represent. Neither the methods nor Appendix I specifies the visit-level, repeated-observation, or aggregation structure. The form acknowledges this discrepancy in measure_detail yet assigns output as a definite observation unit. Under the requirement to verify the actual analysis unit, it remains unconfirmed and should be null; retain 4,997 as the reported observation count without interpreting it as 4,997 distinct ads.
problems.quote: We obtained a sample of 2,000 ads from a total of 11,138 ads, sampling between one and two ads from each of the 1,751 teams.
problems.locator: PDF pp. 18-19, Section 3.9 (field sample and exclusions); p. 20, Section 3.10, Equation 2; p. 25, Table 3, VTD; pp. 49-50, Appendix I; p. 53, Table I, VTD columns 4-6.

problems.source_says: Table I reports 4,997 VTR observations for a field sample of 2,000 ads before exclusions. The paper defines VTR as the fraction of the report viewed and tracks visits through an ad-specific DocSend link. Although Equation 2 indexes ads, the text never reconciles that indexing with the larger number of observations or defines one actual VTR analysis row. The form already notes this source ambiguity, so the definite output unit is not fully verified. Leave the unit null while preserving the reported 4,997 observations; do not guess that a row is an ad, a visitor, or a visit.

problems.locator: PDF pp. 18-19, Section 3.9; p. 20, Section 3.10, Equation 2; pp. 49-50, Appendix I; p. 53, Table I, VTR columns 1-3.

confirmed.statement: Criterion 3 holds: submitted ad copy receives a computed diversity score, and a separate Prolific sample evaluates the produced ads.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 17-18, Section 3.8; p. 21, Section 3.10, Output diversity.

confirmed.statement: All 13 outcomes concern ads produced during the 40-minute collaborative task with AI available in the Human-AI arm. DALL-E 3 image generation was also available to human participants in both arms.

Question coding is supported: S1-O1 is across_people; S1-O2 through S1-O13 are with_ai. Later ratings and field testing evaluate the original ads; they are not new unassisted production after AI removal.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 14-18, Sections 3.3-3.9; p. 21, Output diversity; creativity-codebook.md section 1.

confirmed.statement: S1-O1 compares ad text with its treatment-group centroid across different participants, rather than measuring only variety within one person. Diversity, embedding_similarity, text-embedding-3-small, participant averaging, and N=2,034 are supported.

S1-O1: Table 2 reports intercept 0.303 (SE 0.010), Human-AI -0.094 (SE 0.006), both p<0.001, and 2,034 observations. The delegation result in its notes also matches Table 6: -0.083 (SE 0.012), N=1,222.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 22, Table 2; p. 23, Section 4.1; p. 30, Table 6, Panel B.

confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 17-18, Section 3.8; p. 19, Section 3.10; p. 22, Table 2 notes.

summary: Eligibility holds because submitted ads receive independent ratings and computed diversity scores. Coding is refuted by an unsupported category-count label for completion rates and unresolved analysis units for both field-view outcomes; the reported numbers match the PDF tables.
